summary: A baseline-closed component for one-parameter rational-coefficient polynomial specialization: the regular subring at a point, its evaluation ring map, coefficientwise polynomial specialization, conditional ring laws, a denominator product, degree preservation and simultaneous avoidance of finitely many bad parameters. All seven stages remain open. Hilbert irreducibility, irreducibility preservation, Galois-group preservation, general parameter spaces and the arithmetic fundamental-group programme are explicit remaining work.

nodes.title: Rational functions regular at a point
nodes.statement: For t ∈ K, construct the native subring Rₜ of K(T) whose elements are exactly f with denom(f)(t) ≠ 0, using the monic reduced denominator. Its operations and inclusion are inherited from K(T).
hypotheses: K is an arbitrary field, with no characteristic assumption. T is the rational-function parameter and Y the separate polynomial variable. Additional hypotheses appear in the statement.
proofSteps: Use RatFunc.denom_zero and denom_one for the nullary operations.

RatFunc.denom_add_dvd and denom_mul_dvd reduce closure under addition and multiplication to nonvanishing of the product of the input denominators. Evaluation of a divisor of a polynomial with nonzero value is nonzero.
For negation, write −f = (−num(f))/denom(f) using RatFunc.num_div_denom; RatFunc.denom_dvd shows that denom(−f) divides denom(f). Bundle these closure facts with the native Subring constructor.
acceptance: Reduction must cancel removable factors before deciding regularity.
Rₜ is a subring, and the value zero alone does not certify a pole.

nodes.title: Evaluation on the regular subring
nodes.statement: Construct eₜ : Rₜ → K as a native ring homomorphism, with eₜ(f)=RatFunc.eval(id,t,f). Thus its value is num(f)(t)/denom(f)(t).
hypotheses: K is an arbitrary field, with no characteristic assumption. T is the rational-function parameter and Y the separate polynomial variable. Additional hypotheses appear in the statement.
proofSteps: Use regular-membership to supply the two nonvanishing hypotheses in each of RatFunc.eval_add and eval_mul.
Use RatFunc.eval_zero and eval_one for the remaining homomorphism fields. The underlying function is the existing evaluation, restricted to Rₜ.
acceptance: The evaluation map need not be injective: T−t is in its kernel.
It is surjective since every constant value is attained.

nodes.title: Rational-coefficient polynomial specialization
nodes.statement: For t ∈ K and p=Σₙ cₙ(T)Yⁿ ∈ K(T)[Y], define spₜ(p)=Σₙ RatFunc.eval(id,t,cₙ)Yⁿ ∈ K[Y], using a finite sum over the native support of p. This is a total function. Ring laws are asserted only when all input coefficients are regular at t.
hypotheses: K is an arbitrary field, with no characteristic assumption. T is the rational-function parameter and Y the separate polynomial variable. Additional hypotheses appear in the statement.
proofSteps: Use Polynomial.sum with monomial n (RatFunc.eval(id,t,cₙ)); no new polynomial carrier is introduced.
RatFunc.eval_zero ensures that coefficients outside the original support remain zero. Keep the total coefficient function distinct from the ring map defined on Rₜ.
acceptance: The variable T is replaced by t; the polynomial variable Y is unchanged.
At poles the total function still returns a polynomial, but its multiplication law can fail.

hypotheses: K is an arbitrary field, with no characteristic assumption. T is the rational-function parameter and Y the separate polynomial variable. Additional hypotheses appear in the statement.
proofSteps: Apply Polynomial.coeff_sum and coeff_monomial to the finite defining sum.
At an index in p.support only its own term survives; outside support the coefficient is zero by Polynomial.mem_support_iff and RatFunc.eval_zero.

nodes.title: Specialization preserves addition
nodes.statement: For p,q ∈ K(T)[Y] whose every coefficient has nonzero denominator at t, spₜ(p + q)=spₜ(p) + spₜ(q).
hypotheses: K is an arbitrary field, with no characteristic assumption. T is the rational-function parameter and Y the separate polynomial variable. Additional hypotheses appear in the statement.
proofSteps: Use regular-membership to lift p and q with the existing Polynomial.toSubring; Polynomial.map_toSubring recovers p and q under inclusion.
Apply Polynomial.map_add to the lifted polynomials, then specialization-map-regular to their sum.
Apply Polynomial.map_add for eₜ and identify both factors using specialization-map-regular. No unrestricted ring map K(T) → K is constructed.
acceptance: Every coefficient-regularity hypothesis is retained; the multiplication pole test fails if it is removed.

nodes.title: Denominator product of a polynomial
nodes.statement: For p ∈ K(T)[Y], define D(p) ∈ K[T] to be the product over n ∈ p.support of denom(p.coeff(n)). It is a product with repetitions, not a least common denominator. The empty product for p=0 is one.
hypotheses: K is an arbitrary field, with no characteristic assumption. T is the rational-function parameter and Y the separate polynomial variable. Additional hypotheses appear in the statement.
proofSteps: Use the native finite coefficient support and RatFunc.denom; multiplication occurs in K[T].
The choice of native reduced denominator makes D intrinsic to p. Coefficients that are zero contribute no support index; their denominator would be one.
acceptance: Repeated denominator factors remain repeated in D.
Apparent poles removed by cancellation contribute no factor.

nodes.title: Nonvanishing denominator product
nodes.statement: For every p ∈ K(T)[Y], D(p) is a nonzero polynomial in K[T], including p=0.
hypotheses: K is an arbitrary field, with no characteristic assumption. T is the rational-function parameter and Y the separate polynomial variable. Additional hypotheses appear in the statement.
proofSteps: Every factor is nonzero by RatFunc.denom_ne_zero. A finite product in the domain K[T] is nonzero, with empty product one.
acceptance: This theorem does not say D(p)(t) is nonzero at every t.

nodes.title: The exact coefficient-regularity locus
nodes.statement: For all p ∈ K(T)[Y] and t ∈ K, D(p)(t) ≠ 0 if and only if denom(p.coeff(n))(t) ≠ 0 for every n ∈ ℕ.
hypotheses: K is an arbitrary field, with no characteristic assumption. T is the rational-function parameter and Y the separate polynomial variable. Additional hypotheses appear in the statement.
proofSteps: Polynomial.eval_prod turns D(p)(t) into a finite product of denominator values. A product over a field is nonzero exactly when each factor is nonzero.
Outside p.support the coefficient is zero, so RatFunc.denom_zero supplies denominator one. Extend the finite conjunction to all n.
acceptance: For p=0 the equivalence has two true sides.

nodes.title: Degree preservation by the leading coefficient
nodes.statement: If RatFunc.eval(id,t,leadingCoeff(p)) ≠ 0, then natDegree(spₜ(p))=natDegree(p). This sufficient condition needs no additional hypothesis on lower coefficients for the total coefficient function.
hypotheses: K is an arbitrary field, with no characteristic assumption. T is the rational-function parameter and Y the separate polynomial variable. Additional hypotheses appear in the statement.
proofSteps: Above natDegree(p), Polynomial.coeff_eq_zero_of_natDegree_lt and RatFunc.eval_zero make all specialized coefficients zero; apply Polynomial.natDegree_le_iff_coeff_eq_zero.
At natDegree(p), specialization-coefficients identifies the coefficient with the assumed nonzero leading-coefficient value. Apply Polynomial.natDegree_eq_of_le_of_coeff_ne_zero.
acceptance: TY+1 at t=0 fails the hypothesis and loses degree.
At a regular point a vanishing leading coefficient can give a lower-degree irreducible polynomial; irreducibility alone does not preserve degree.

nodes.title: A polynomial guard for regular specialization
nodes.statement: If (D(p)·num(leadingCoeff(p)))(t) ≠ 0, then every coefficient of p is regular at t and natDegree(spₜ(p))=natDegree(p).
hypotheses: K is an arbitrary field, with no characteristic assumption. T is the rational-function parameter and Y the separate polynomial variable. Additional hypotheses appear in the statement.
proofSteps: The nonzero product value gives D(p)(t) ≠ 0 and num(leadingCoeff(p))(t) ≠ 0. Apply denominator-product-domain.
Apply coefficient regularity at n=natDegree(p) to its leading coefficient. The defining fraction in RatFunc.eval is nonzero since both numerator and denominator values are nonzero.
Apply specialization-degree.
acceptance: For p=TY+1 the guard includes T, so t=0 is excluded.
The guard ensures degree and regularity; it does not ensure irreducibility.

nodes.title: Finiteness of bad specialization parameters
nodes.statement: For nonzero p ∈ K(T)[Y], the set of t ∈ K where either a coefficient has a pole or natDegree(spₜ(p)) differs from natDegree(p) is finite.
hypotheses: K is an arbitrary field, with no characteristic assumption. T is the rational-function parameter and Y the separate polynomial variable. Additional hypotheses appear in the statement.
proofSteps: The polynomial G=D(p)·num(leadingCoeff(p)) is nonzero: use denominator-product-nonzero, Polynomial.leadingCoeff_ne_zero and RatFunc.num_ne_zero.
The contrapositive of specialization-guard puts every bad parameter in the root set of G.
Apply Polynomial.finite_setOfPred_isRoot and Set.Finite.subset. This is valid over finite fields too, without asserting existence of a good parameter.
acceptance: Y²−T is regular and degree two at every t, although its irreducibility changes.
Over F₂, (T²−T)Y+1 loses degree at every parameter; finiteness remains true.

nodes.title: Simultaneous avoidance for a finite polynomial family
nodes.statement: Let K be infinite, s a finite set of nonzero polynomials in K(T)[Y], and A a finite subset of K. There exists t ∈ K outside A such that every coefficient of every p ∈ s is regular at t and every spₜ(p) has the same natural degree as p.
hypotheses: K is an arbitrary field, with no characteristic assumption. T is the rational-function parameter and Y the separate polynomial variable. Additional hypotheses appear in the statement.
proofSteps: For each p ∈ s, finite-bad-specializations supplies a finite bad set. Induct on s using Set.Finite.union to unite them and A.
Use Set.Finite.exists_notMem in the infinite field K to choose t outside that union. Its nonmembership gives each regularity and degree assertion.
acceptance: The empty family reduces to avoiding A.
The statement must not be read as preserving irreducibility, prescribed Galois groups or linear disjointness.

researchNotes.nativeReuse: Read the reviewed AUDIT-09 evidence before planning. Read all cited baseline declarations at their pins. Native RatFunc evaluation, Polynomial.toSubring and its degree/map API are reused. No matching regular-at-a-point specialization component was found in the two pinned libraries. Broader generic localization, Galois-category classification and rational-map specialization remain their native or owning-roadmap work.
researchNotes.upstreamSearch: On 2026-09-27 GitHub open-PR searches for Hilbertian and title specialization returned no matches; RatFunc in:title returned #31603 (head c3c4dd2bc13e0711723f507b24e7bf97e21f527f), whose full description proposes replacing RatFunc by a FractionRing abbreviation. The design retains the public RatFunc API and makes no competing fraction-field carrier. researchNotes.relatedOwners: ArithmeticDynamics:DY.6 specializes projective rational maps using a resultant and primitive homogeneous lifts; it does not supply this affine coefficient-ring interface. DT.5 defines regular Mahler points along an infinite orbit, and CA.2 rational power series. Their carriers and outputs are not reconstructed here.
researchNotes.readBoundary: Only the source sections listed in sources were inspected for this checkpoint. Serre was acquired as a lead but not substantively read and is not a source citation. SGA1, NSW, the Hurwitz-space references, the Hilbert–Dörge proof and Chapter 9 require full proof reading. The six routed Harpaz–Wittenberg obligations were checked on author-copy pp.28–31 and retained verbatim in scope, without claiming their prerequisite proofs.
researchNotes.conventions: One rational parameter T, one polynomial variable Y, arbitrary field K. Infinite K is required only in simultaneous existence. The denominator product is not a least common denominator. No generic irreducibility, separability, degree-positive, characteristic-zero or Hilbertian hypothesis is smuggled into the elementary specialization component.
